entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Sambhaji, also known as Shambhuraje, ascended to the throne as the second Chhatrapati (king) of the nascent Maratha Empire in 1681, inheriting a powerful but embattled state carved out by his father, Shivaji, across the Deccan Plateau of India. His eight-year reign, from 1681 until his execution in 1689, was defined by relentless military campaigns against the formidable Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb, who sought to crush the Maratha state and annex the entire Deccan. Sambhaji's strategic leadership and military prowess, particularly in naval warfare and fort defense, were crucial in consolidating Maratha independence and preventing the immediate collapse of the empire in the face of overwhelming imperial might, thereby preserving the foundations for its later expansion.

Upon Shivaji's death in April 1680, Sambhaji had to swiftly suppress a succession dispute, imprisoning his stepmother Soyarabai and half-brother Rajaram I to secure his claim by January 1681. His reign was almost entirely consumed by warfare against Aurangzeb, who personally led the Mughal Deccan campaign with an army estimated at 500,000 men. Sambhaji successfully repelled numerous Mughal invasions, notably defending the strategically vital fort of Raigad and engaging in naval skirmishes along the Konkan coast against both the Mughals and the Portuguese. He also launched campaigns against the Siddis of Janjira and the Portuguese in Goa, expanding Maratha influence and revenues through continued raids and the collection of Chauth.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Sambhaji's eight-year reign was pivotal in consolidating the nascent Maratha Empire against overwhelming Mughal aggression, ensuring its survival and setting the stage for the subsequent 27-year war that ultimately weakened the Mughal Empire. His resistance directly contributed to the Marathas' eventual rise as a dominant Indian power.
